title: Rav Ada

paragraphs: We find Rabbi Abba bar Rav Ada: [Shabbat 130a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.130a.18). Rabbi Chanina son of Rav Ada: [Shir HaShirim Rabbah, on “For better”](https://www.sefaria.org/Shir_HaShirim_Rabbah.1.2.7); and in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 4:4, Rabbi Chananyah son of Rav Ada. Mar bar Rav Ada: Shabbat 140b (Hyman’s reference; compare [140a:17](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.140a.17)). Rava and Ravin bar Rav Ada: [Beitzah 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.33b.6). Rabbah bar Rav Ada: [Sukkah 3a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.3a.1).[^1]

notes.text: The consulted [Shir HaShirim Rabbah](https://www.sefaria.org/Shir_HaShirim_Rabbah.1.2.7) calls Chanina the son of Rabbi Ada. In [Shabbat 140a:17](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.140a.17), an alternate reading gives the school of Mar bar Rav Ada. [Beitzah 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.33b.6) names both Rava and Ravin, while [Sukkah 3a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.3a.1) names Rabbah. The [Seder HaDorot entry under Rav Ada](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=248&lang=en) lists several of these names as alternatives. The passages leave the relationships among these occurrences open.
